reason: E3 directly shows that a high-entropy oxide support (HEFO) stabilizes single-atom Pd against sintering, maintains CO oxidation activity after hydrothermal aging and in 10 vol% H2O, and forms activated Oβ. E2 demonstrates structural stability of a high-entropy oxide support up to 850 °C, supporting durability. However, no cited evidence addresses resistance to NO poisoning, and E1 discusses conventional mixed-oxide supports, not high-entropy oxides, so it does not directly support the key premises.
premises: High-entropy oxide supports stabilize highly dispersed active sites and resist nanoparticle sintering.
High-entropy oxide supports increase oxygen mobility and form activated surface chemisorbed oxygen (Oβ).
High-entropy oxide supports resist poisoning by H2O and NO.
High-entropy oxide supports improve long-term durability under hydrothermal aging.
